//: One composite index, for searching by name.
Firestore builds a single-field index for every field by itself, and a
query with one equality filter and a limit is served by those. A query
that filters on one field and orders by another is not, and until the
index exists that query fails outright - while publishing, which needs no
index at all, keeps working. That combination is miserable: a library you
can publish to and never see anything in.
So browsing and 'published by me' were rewritten to use one filter and sort
in the browser, and they work on a fresh project with nothing set up here.
Searching by name genuinely needs public + nameLower together, because the
rules require the public filter for the query to be provably safe and the
prefix match needs the ordering. That is the one below.
